description: The world's terrain, made by tools/terrain.py from world/terrain-inputs.json (O152): per 3.5 km square of the world model's grid the kind and the country, per square corner the height in metres, the main river's squares with their water level (source to mouth) and the estuary's squares; the border on the water (the river from the crossing, then the estuary's axis to the open bay; a line in squares, x, y); the rapids above Ferrano (the river's squares through them: the barges stay below); the border crossing on the river; streams for the printed map and the small brooks it shows as well; the rivers the encyclopedia names (every stream whose basin reaches 1,000 km2 on the mainland or 500 km2 on Lisavu, from its source to the sea or the larger river it joins, the larger branch keeping the name at each confluence: its course in squares, length, basin, source height, the countries of its squares, and the river it joins; the raster world/terrain/*-basins.png gives each fine cell the river whose course its water reaches first); the managed forests (their compartments of 875 m and the age of each); the fine rasters in world/terrain/. Do not edit: change the inputs and run the script.

lumeport.note: Lumeport's brook (O153): it rises in the low hills west of the centre and runs through the town to the open bay on its east shore; the town's first fresh water. Shown on the map although it drains less than the streams it shows.

managed_forests.name: Upland State Forest
managed_forests.note: The managed forest of Upland State (O152 audit, owner 2026-11-18): a state forest planted on the slopes north of Marrowdale, where the upland falls towards the town, on ground too steep for the best fields; the sawmill at Marrowdale (36-xb) buys its logs here. Its land is forest whatever the landscape made it; it is worked in compartments of 875 m (the cells of the cover raster), each of one age: felled and replanted, young, pole and mature stands, felled in turn over the rotation (ages from seed). polygon: the forest's edge in squares (x, y).
